THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both the counsels, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous second appeal is preferred by the claimant-land loser contending that the land bearing Survey No.64/1 of Kadboor Village measuring 3 acre 12 guntas belong to the appellant, was acquired by the respondents by notification dated 09.08.1984 passed under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for the purpose of construction of Bennitora Project.
The Land Acquisition Officer has passed an award on 30.09.1987 awarding compensation of Rs.3,500/- per acre for dry land.
Aggrieved by the same, appellant sought reference of the order to Civil Court, and on reference, the Civil Judge has awarded compensation of Rs.12,200/- per acre.
Aggrieved by the same, the appellant preferred an appeal before the first Appellate Court.
The first Appellate Court NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 enhanced the compensation to Rs.74,800/- per acre.
Being not satisfied with the said judgment and award, appellant has preferred this second appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in respect of acquisition of land of the same village under same notification for the same purpose, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MSA Nos.200055/2018 (LAC) clubbed with MSA Nos.200061/2018 and 200063/2018 dated 15.06.2021,
has awarded compensation of Rs.1,14,773/- per acre.
He further submits that the Karnataka Neeravari Nigama Limited is not a party in LAC or LACA Court and they are also not party in the MSA Nos.200055/2018 and connected matters stated supra.
He further submits that as on the date of 4(1) notification, the KNNL was not in existence and hence they are not beneficiary as on the date of notification.
Therefore, the question of impleading them as party to the proceedings does not arise.
Even the Government has not raised this objection in the above stated cases.
Therefore, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 Government has no locus standi to raise this objection at this stage.
4. Learned High Court Government Pleader has not disputed the said fact.
The respondents have not challenged the award passed by this Court in the above cases and the same has attained finality as the respondents have already satisfied the award in those cases.
However, he fairly submits that the beneficiary is necessary and proper party to the proceedings but the appellant has not impleaded the KNNL as party.
Hence, the appeal is not maintainable.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the following points would arise for consideration:
1) Whether the appeal is maintainable in the absence of Karnataka Neeravari Nigama Limited as party to the proceedings?

sentences.text: 2 2) Whether the appellants are entitled for compensation as per the award passed in MSA Nos.200055/2018 (LAC) clubbed with NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 MSA Nos.200061/2018 and 200063/2018 dated 15.06.2021 as the land in question involved in the present case and the aforesaid cases are one and the same?
3) What order or award?

6. My answer to the above points are:
Point No.1: In the Negative.
Point No.2: In the affirmative.
Point No.3: As per final order.

Regarding point No.1:
7.

I have carefully examined the material on record and also the judgment and award dated 01.08.1996 passed in LAC No.165/1995 on the file of the Principal Civil Judge at Gulbarga, wherein the Special Land Acquisition Officer, MIP, Gulbarga, is the only party to the proceedings.

A perusal of LACA No.199 and 200 of 2014, reveals that the Special Land Acquisition Officer, M & MIP,
Gulbarga, and Deputy Commissioner, Kalaburagi, are the parties to the proceedings.
In both the cases, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 Government has not raised any objections to implead the KNNL as party in the aforesaid proceedings.
Now for the first time, the learned High Court Government Pleader has raised this objection.

When the KNNL was not in existence and was not beneficiary as on the date of 4(1) notification, the question of impleading them is not required and the learned High Court Government Pleader has not placed any material to show that the KNNL is necessary and proper party to the present appeal.
Respondent have not taken necessary legal steps to implead KNNL till this day.
Hence, the KNNL is not required to adjudicate the matter in dispute.

In this regard, I rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satish Kumar Gupta And Etc. Etc Vs State Of Haryana And Ors. Etc reported in AIR 2017 SC 1072, wherein it is observed that post acquisition, allottee has no locus standi to be heard in the matter and is neither a necessary nor proper party.

entities.text: Satish Kumar Gupta And Etc. Etc Vs State Of Haryana And Ors. Etc reported in AIR 2017 SC 1072
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid finding, I am of the considered opinion that at that this stage,
Karnataka Neeravari Nigama Limited is not necessary and proper NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 party to this proceeding.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the negative.

Regarding point No.2:
8.

The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has passed an order in MSA No.200055/2018 (LAC) connected with MSA No.200061/2018 and MSA No.200063/2018 disposed of on 15.06.2021 with regard to lands which are acquired under same notification dated 09.08.1984 for same purpose.
The same is not challenged by respondent/s.
Therefore, in view of the judgment rendered by the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court which has determined the value of the similar land, it is relevant to consider and determine the market value.

The same can be relied for fixing the market value of the land in question acquired for the same Annappa S/O Sharanappa vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54455022/
3 purpose which, admittedly are dry lands.

sentences.text: Therefore, in view of discussion made above relying on the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MSA No.200055/2018 (LAC) connected with MSA No.200061/2018 and MSA No.200063/2018 disposed of on NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 15.06.2021, the appellant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,14,773/- per acre in respect of the acquired land, with all statutory benefits.
Accordingly, I answer point No.2 in the affirmative.

Regarding point No.3:
9.
In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The appeal is allowed with costs.

The impugned judgment and award in LACA No.200/2014 passed by the I-Additional District Judge at Kalaburagi is modified as under:
(i) The appellant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,14,773/- per acre in respect of acquired land with all statutory benefits.

However, the appellant is not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation for the period of delay in filing this appeal as well as the appeal before the First Appellate Court.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:2192 (ii) The appellant is granted six weeks time to make good the deficit Court fee.
